title: Gallantt Ispat Ltd - 532726 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Gallantt Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 203 crore (18% margin) from INR 254 crore a year ago, though flat sequentially, on coal costs and a pellet plant shutdown.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2% year-on-year to INR 1,146 crore but fell from INR 1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was INR 203 crore (18% margin) versus INR 209 crore in Q4 and INR 254 crore in Q1 FY26, and PAT was INR 124 crore (11% margin). Management attributed the year-on-year decline to higher raw material costs (up 9%), the planned pellet plant shutdown, a seasonal monsoon-driven TMT price correction, and higher employee costs. The 1.23 million tonne capacity expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively.

segments.name: TMT / long products (Gorakhpur and Gujarat)
segments.commentary: TMT sales volume was flat YoY at about 192,000 tonnes and down about 8% QoQ against a strong Q4 FY26. Gorakhpur rolling mill utilisation is 93%, while Kutch is at about 66%.

segments.name: Pellet and sponge iron
segments.commentary: External sales fell YoY and QoQ due to higher captive consumption for DRI and steelmaking, plus the planned pellet plant shutdown, which is now complete.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: Billet volumes grew 13% YoY and 38% QoQ, running ahead of internal plans for the year.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes (0.23 million tonnes) under the INR 3,000 crore capex programme is expected to commission in H2 FY27, with benefits flowing from H2.
Pellet plant returns to normal captive utilisation in the coming quarter now the shutdown is complete; management expects no substantial EBITDA erosion through the year.
Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted because of the monsoon; management expects Q3 and Q4 to pick up.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-9% this year; management referred to 8-9% in the Q&A.
Captive iron ore mines (UP and Rajasthan) are targeted to commence production in FY28; UP exploration expected to finish in 2-3 months and Rajasthan in about six months.
Solar: 18 MW in Gujarat due for Q2 FY27 and 60 MW at Gorakhpur due for Q4 FY27 (the call also cites 67 MW elsewhere, so the split is unclear).
Debottlenecking at Gujarat unit to complete within FY27.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about INR 3,000 crore, of which about INR 800 crore spent over FY26 and Q1 FY27; INR 137 crore spent in Q1 FY27. Funded by internal accruals with no term loans planned.
Roughly half of capex goes to mining: three iron ore mines (two in UP, one in Rajasthan), with beneficiation plants in UP and a beneficiation-cum-pellet plant in Rajasthan. Production from FY28.
Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes, commissioning in H2 FY27.
Solar: 7 MW trial plant commissioned in FY26; 18 MW in Gujarat (Q2 FY27); 60 MW at Gorakhpur (Q4 FY27). Total about 85 MW.
Pellet plant installed capacity about 8 lakh tonnes against raw feed need of 9-9.5 lakh tonnes a year.
demand_pricing: TMT and rebar prices corrected meaningfully during the quarter from a firm start; management said the correction was seasonal and sector-wide, with flat products holding up better.
India turned a net steel importer in the quarter, with imports rising under some free trade routes; the industry has sought anti-dumping duties alongside existing safeguard duties.
Management claims a market share above 25% in its addressable UP market and cites brand marketing with celebrity endorsements (Ajay Devgn, and now Janhvi Kapoor).
Export: management said exports are not a focus. Gorakhpur is inland, and Gujarat billet exports happen only occasionally.

Raw material mix: Gorakhpur coal is 100% linkage for power plant; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian and the rest South African, sourced via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal for power and South African coal for process.
